figures.cap: building, window and car with 40 degree angle of depression

parts.latex:
The angle of depression from a window to a car on the ground is $40^\circ$.

The car is 50 metres from the base of the building.

\exfigure{719_q10_1}

How high above the ground is the base of the window, correct to the nearest metre?

solutions.latex:
The horizontal dashed line is parallel to the ground, so the angle of elevation from the car to the window is also $40^\circ$ (alternate angles).

In the right-angled triangle, the side opposite $40^\circ$ is the height $h$ and the adjacent side is $50$ m, so use $\tan$.
$$\begin{aligned} \tan 40^\circ &= \dfrac{h}{50} \\ h &= 50\tan 40^\circ \\ &\approx 41.95 \\ &\approx 42 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is option C.

6162.stem:
Robert walks 5.59 km from his house to the shop on a bearing of 063°. He then turns on a bearing of 124° to walk to the post office, where he is 13.34 km from home.

\exfigure{719_q22_1}

figures.cap: bearing diagram House, Shop, Post office
solution sketch: bearing diagram annotated with angles x, y, 56 degrees, 27 degrees

parts.latex: Find the true bearing of Robert’s house from the post office.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{719_q22_s1}

Let $x$ and $y$ be the angles at $S$ on either side of the north line through $S$, so $\angle HSP = x + y$.
$$y = 180 - 124 = 56^\circ$$
$$x = 63^\circ \quad (\text{alternate angles, parallel north lines})$$
$$\begin{aligned} \angle HSP &= 56 + 63 \\ &= 119^\circ \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none). Source drawing kept.

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule in triangle $HSP$, with $Z = \angle HPS$:
$$\dfrac{\sin Z}{5.59} = \dfrac{\sin 119^\circ}{13.34}$$
$$\begin{aligned} Z &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5.59 \sin 119^\circ}{13.34}\right) \\ &= 21.49\ldots \\ &\approx 21^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing of } H \text{ from } P &= 360 - (56 + 21) \\ &= 283^\circ\text{T} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the sine rule, or equivalent merit
